blocks.content:
At-mentions tell Assistant which data source, dashboard, or panel to use. Without a mention, Assistant may pick a data source for you or ask for more detail. With a mention, you point it at the right place so answers are more accurate.

Use this rule when you choose:

- **Mention** when you already know which data source (or dashboard/panel) should answer the question.
- **Omit** when you are exploring what is available and do not have a target yet.
- **Retry with a mention** when a reply ignored the source you meant, or stayed too generic.

Here you send a vague prompt first, then the same kind of request with an at-mention so you can compare focus.

whenTrue.content: If this guide is docked in the sidebar, pop it out into a floating window so it stays visible beside **Assistant**.

blocks.content: To see why at-mentions help, complete the following steps:
Open **Assistant** from the top toolbar (sparkle icon) if the panel is closed.
blocks.hint: Skip if Assistant is already open from the previous milestone.

blocks.content:
In the chat input, paste or type a vague prompt (no at-mention):

> Show me something useful from my stack

Or try:

> What can you tell me about my data sources?

In a new message, type the at symbol (@) in the chat input.

Pick a data source from the mention list (or type the name after the at symbol). Prefer one you already know from this path, for example a Prometheus or Loki source.

Finish the prompt so it uses that mention.

Example shapes (replace the mention with yours):

> Summarize what I can query from @prometheus-ds

> Show recent activity from @loki-logs

> List metrics available in @grafanacloud-usage

Compare the two replies for focus, not perfection:

- The **mentioned** reply should center on the data source you picked (name it, query it, or stay clearly scoped to it).
- The **vague** reply may roam, pick a different source, or ask for more detail.

If the mentioned reply is clearer, keep using `@` when you know the target. If you only needed a tour of what exists, omitting `@` is fine.

You practiced turning a vague request into a targeted one with an at-mention, and when to mention versus explore without one.

For more examples, refer to [Use mentions for better results](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/machine-learning/assistant/get-started/grafana-cloud/#use-mentions-for-better-results).
